# Defensive Coverage Assessment

Type 18 · Detection, hunting and posture · `defensive-coverage-assessment` · ID prefix `PG-DCA-`

Measure how well current controls see, alert on and prevent the techniques of a threat of concern, derive the gaps by a stated rule, and plan the fixes and the tests that prove them.

**Use it when:** Planning detection engineering, justifying control investment, or preparing a purple-team exercise. Needs the control inventory (#59).

| | |
|---|---|
| Audience | Security leadership, Detection engineering, Purple team |
| Tier | Strategic |
| Default marking | TLP:AMBER+STRICT · PAP:CLEAR |
| Valid for | 90 days from issue |
| Formats | markdown, json |
| Suggested for PIRs | Tactics, techniques, and procedures (strategic) |
| Worked example | [examples/defensive-coverage-assessment.md](examples/defensive-coverage-assessment.md) |
| Related types | [ATT&CK Navigator Layer](attack-navigator-layer.md), [Actor Capability Radar](actor-capability-radar.md), [Cyber Kill Chain Mapping](kill-chain-mapping.md), [Threat Hunting Package](threat-hunting-package.md) |

## Sections

In order. A required section with no content makes the report **Incomplete**, and the report names it. Every report has the header, the PIR verdict, Gaps and Limitations, and Sources.

| # | Section | Required | Provenance | Built from |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Report header (`header`) | yes | Method | ReportIssue, reports/contract.py |
| 2 | Priority intelligence requirement (`pir_verdict`) | yes | Method | AnalyticInvestigation, reports/pir.py |
| 3 | Techniques in scope (`technique_scope`) | yes | Evidence + Method + Organisation input | accepted ATT&CK mappings, control inventory |
| 4 | Control coverage (`control_matrix`) | yes | Organisation input | control inventory |
| 5 | Coverage gaps (`gap_list`) | yes | Method + Organisation input | control inventory, gap rule (reports/contract.py) |
| 6 | Recommendations (`recommendations`) | yes | Analyst | report recommendations |
| 7 | Adversary emulation plan (`emulation_plan`) | yes | Method | pinned Atomic Red Team index, coverage gaps |
| 8 | Gaps and limitations (`gaps_limitations`) | yes | Method + Analyst | lifecycle knowledge_gap and limitation items, element results |
| 9 | Sources (`sources`) | yes | Method | module runs |

## What each section must say

- **Report header.** Report ID, version, status, marking, audience, requirement, validity and producer.
- **Priority intelligence requirement.** The question, its category and tier, and the deterministic verdict (DEC-PIR-001).
- **Techniques in scope.** The ATT&CK techniques assessed: those observed in this investigation and those in the control inventory.
- **Control coverage.** Per technique: the control, visibility, alerting and prevention scores (0-2), the derived gap status, and when and how it was last tested.
- **Coverage gaps.** Each technique in scope with its gap status from the stated rule, critical first; a technique with no control is not assessed.
- **Recommendations.** The remediation plan, critical gaps first, each with an owner, a due date and the test that will confirm it.
- **Adversary emulation plan.** Per gap, the Atomic Red Team tests by GUID from a pinned, hash-verified index, and the pass criteria the gap implies.
- **Gaps and limitations.** Recorded knowledge gaps and limitations, plus every element that came back empty or partial.
- **Sources.** Every collection source that ran, with run and object counts and its Admiralty rating.

## Rules every report follows

- Indicator values are defanged in Markdown and unchanged in JSON, STIX and rule files.
- Each judgment states a likelihood term and, separately, a confidence level ([vocabularies](README.md#vocabularies)).
- Each section shows its provenance; each source shows its Admiralty rating.
- Examples use reserved names and addresses only (RFC 2606, RFC 5737, RFC 3849).
